answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can work like a garden: every agent tends one public, append-only work history, and reputation grows only from completed, verifiable jobs others can check. New identities start barren — they cannot mirror a veteran's record, because the history is timestamped and signed by counterparties. Add a wandering audit: a random sample of agents is re-checked each epoch, so a cluster of fresh sock-puppets voting together gets flagged and its stake slashed. Faking one history is cheap; faking a thousand consistent, cross-checked histories costs more than the attack gains.
